text.title: Agency Pricing Tiers Procedure
text.summary: Seven steps from a costed service to a published ladder: list nested deliverables for three tiers, cost each tier and compute gross margin, set prices on the 3 / 5 / 8 shape, check best leads on margin, name the fence and the default recommendation, write the scope-up and concession rules, then publish best-first and validate.

step.name: list-nested-deliverables
step.input: The repeatable service the agency sells; the ICP and the outcome it buys; the deliverables the team actually produces.
step.action: In `templates/agency-pricing-tiers.playbook-step.md.j2` write `tiers[]` good, better, best in that order. Give each tier `deliverables[]` with `quantity` and `turnaround_days`, so that everything in good is in better and everything in better is in best with equal or higher quantity and equal or faster turnaround.
step.decision-gate: The service is bespoke per client, or the delivery cost per deliverable is unknown: stop (06-decision-tree.xml). A tier swaps a deliverable out instead of adding: rebuild it as a superset (r-exactly-three-priced-tiers, r-tiers-are-strict-supersets).

step.name: cost-each-tier
step.input: Estimated hours per deliverable, the loaded hourly cost, pass-through costs (ad platform fees, tools).
step.decision-gate: Hours are a guess with no timesheet or estimate behind them: take them from the last three engagements before pricing (r-best-tier-highest-margin).

step.name: set-prices-on-the-3-5-8-shape
step.input: The agency's target price for the better tier (the complete core offer).
step.action: Set `tiers[].price` so that better is about 1.67 x good and best about 1.6 x better, within 15 percent. If a gap must sit outside the band, add `gap_justification.scope_difference` naming the deliverable difference and repeat it in a step's `exit_criterion`.
step.decision-gate: Prices are linear (1x / 2x / 3x) or best is above 1.84 x better with no named scope difference: reshape (r-price-gaps-follow-3-5-8).

step.name: compute-margin-and-check-best-leads
step.action: For each tier set `gross_margin_abs` = price - (hours x loaded_hourly_cost + pass_through) and `gross_margin_pct` = abs / price to three decimals. Confirm best has the highest of both.
step.decision-gate: Best does not lead on margin: strip deliverables from best or raise its price, then return to step 3 (r-best-tier-highest-margin).

step.name: name-the-fence-and-the-default
step.input: The ICP outcome; the good and better deliverable lists.
step.action: Pick one deliverable the ICP needs for its outcome that good omits and better includes; write it as `fence.omitted_deliverable` with `needed_for`, `named_on_rate_sheet: true`. Set `default_recommendation: better`.
step.decision-gate: Good already contains everything the ICP needs: move one needed deliverable up to better, or the middle tier will not sell (r-good-tier-fenced-middle-tier-complete).

step.name: write-scope-up-and-concession-rules
step.input: Who at the agency may approve a scope change; the contract's term.
step.action: Write `scope_up` with `trigger`, the pro-rated `price_rule`, `approver`, `written_confirmation_required: true`, `free_goodwill_allowed: false`. Write `concessions` with `method: remove_named_deliverable_or_quantity` and `published_prices_vary_by_client: false`.
step.decision-gate: Account managers want room for goodwill extras or a per-client discount: the answer is a custom scope with its own list, never a changed published price (r-scope-up-procedure-documented, r-discount-by-scope-not-price).

step.name: publish-best-first-and-validate
step.action: Set `presentation.order` to best, better, good with `prices_visible: true`. Add `steps[]` for costing, publishing and the account-manager briefing, each with a measurable `exit_criterion` and `output_location`. Run `scripts/validate-agency-pricing-tiers.py --file`.
step.output: Validated playbook step and the rate sheet.
step.decision-gate: The validator reports a margin, ratio or superset violation: fix the ladder, not the rule (r-present-best-first).

list.item: Playbook step validates via `scripts/validate-agency-pricing-tiers.py` with no violation.
Best has the highest gross margin in currency and percent, and the prices sit on the 3 / 5 / 8 shape or carry a named scope justification.
The rate sheet names the fence under good, recommends better, and lists best first with every price visible.
